originalTitle: An immortal host has arbitrarily late private blocker services
originalStatement: Immortal-host positive tokens inject into distinct later same-host blocker-service cells.
originalHypotheses: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and the named banked lemmas in the source.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: There are infinitely many blockers by the exact square certificate. Distinct blocker victims give arbitrarily large victim indexes; hence infinitely many lie to the right of any fixed immortal physical host h.
For each such p, host h is live at row p and lies left of its unique victim. Its row-p award is greater than p, so MEX forces a prior private p service at h; p cannot be a diagonal seed.
Cell reach f(t,h)≤t+h+1 implies p>N+h+1 cannot be served at any t≤N. Thus private blocker services at h occur arbitrarily late.

Enumerate the tagged positive tokens associated with h and recursively choose a service after the preceding chosen date and the current token date. This is an injective, forward, same-host assignment. Different hosts use different service cells.

Chosen blockers need not be free B0, and service delays are uncontrolled. Every immortal host h<a also serves d(a) before its numerical deadline, so it cannot be a W endpoint for a blocker owner. This follows by live MEX at d(a), no current diagonal-deadline occurrence and seed exclusion.
